None of the three solutions is correct. The correct count is 3^2025, which none of them gives. I read the problem as follows, and my argument is a sketch rather than a full proof.

**Setup.** I take every layer to have the same total width, so each brick in layer n has width 1/(2^n − 1). Two bricks in adjacent layers share a side exactly when their horizontal intervals overlap in a segment of positive length.

**Overlap count.** Let a = 2^n − 1 be the number of bricks in layer n, and b = 2a + 1 the number in layer n+1. Here gcd(a, b) = 1, so no brick boundary in layer n coincides with one in layer n+1 apart from the two ends of the wall. The number of adjacent-layer pairs that share a side is then a + b − 1 = 3a.

**Each brick has exactly 3 bricks below it.** A brick in layer n has width b/a = 2 + 1/a measured in layer-(n+1) brick widths. Since this exceeds 2, it overlaps at least 3 bricks below. The total is 3a over a bricks, so every brick overlaps exactly 3.

**Check.** The top brick overlaps all 3 bricks of layer 2. Each layer-2 brick overlaps exactly 3 of the 7 bricks of layer 3, giving 9 paths to layer 3.

**Conclusion.** Every brick has exactly 3 choices at each step, and there are 2025 moves, so the number of sequences is 3^2025.

**The three solutions.**
- Solution 1 gives 2^2025, which assumes a half-brick offset between layers. That contradicts the brick counts in the problem.
- Solution 2 gives 1, which assumes all bricks have the same width in every layer. That is impossible with 2^n − 1 bricks per layer.
- Solution 3 gives C(2025, 1012), which assumes a running-bond pattern. That is also inconsistent with the brick counts.

CHOICE: NONE
